title: Five Pairs, One Exit
text:
Rimewall had five roads out and an enemy army on each one.

Sera stood over Jin’s map while winter rain worked through the fortress roof. The Black March had already surrendered the outer wall, two supply basins and every position wide enough for Maedra Dravaryn to turn wounded formations into crimson roads. Behind them waited hospital columns, broken siege crews and the remnants of armies that had learned how much ground a Paragon could make meaningless.

[[speaker:jin]]“We do not need five victories.”

[[speaker:sera]]“We need five exits that remain open long enough to become one retreat.”

She assigned the partnerships by function. Kael and Arin would cut the eastern siege network. Liang and Yun would identify the road seals closing the centre. Lei and Luo would keep the medical corridor moving. Rui and Ilyra would preserve the fleet road. Jin and Mo received the smallest enemy formation: six thousand Haldren spears holding a narrow southern pass.

Mo looked at the map.

[[speaker:mo]]“You gave Wuyue’s number three the weakest battlefield.”

[[speaker:jin]]“I gave you the only battlefield we may remove without winning a fight.”

Haldren’s Ash-Horn Spears had marched beneath Veyrhald’s Gate Seal. Their oldest oath bound them to lawful continental defence. Maedra’s latest order required them to abandon the pass, enter a Hearth settlement and hold civilians inside the route Sera needed.

Mo carried the original oath into the rain beneath a white cloth. Jin remained beyond spear range and changed headquarters before Solveig could turn one genuine footprint into a path toward his body.

Kellan Haldren met Mo before six thousand lowered spearheads.

[[speaker:kellan]]“You crossed into Isgard with an army.”

[[speaker:mo]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:kellan]]“You broke our gates.”

[[speaker:mo]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:kellan]]“And now you lecture us on law?”

Mo unfolded the oath.

[[speaker:mo]]“No. I ask whether Maedra’s private road can command what your ancestors gave to Veyrhald’s public seal.”

Behind Kellan, the Ash-Horn formation remained perfect. That perfection was the point. Haldren had not joined the coalition for rank or revenge. It had obeyed a structure whose legal boundary Maedra now treated as inconvenient.

A messenger reached Kellan with a new order: enter the Hearth, remove its residents and burn the southern stores before Wuyue could take them. Aldric’s Gate Seal did not appear beneath it.

Kellan read the order twice.

Then he turned his spear sideways.

Six thousand weapons followed.

Haldren did not join Wuyue. It did not surrender its arms or apologize for the soldiers it had killed. It withdrew from the Hearth road and demanded a Veyrhald hearing.

One support vanished beneath Isgard’s stronger banners without Sera spending a single life to remove it.

Across Rimewall, four other roads erupted at once.

Sera felt the distances separating every pair and understood what Jin’s map had concealed: none could reach another before their own people died. Rhen’s **Sanctuary of Petals** could not cover all five fronts. Her strength could not become five bodies.

[[speaker:sera]]“The exits hold independently. Nobody abandons their assigned civilians to rescue a ranking.”

Five acknowledgements returned through broken signal lamps.

The gates opened.

Wuyue began the retreat through five battles no pair could afford to lose.

title: Jin Cannot Spend Mo’s Citizens
text:
Jin’s first retreat plan required four thousand imperial soldiers to remain behind.

He did not call it sacrifice. The order named them rear brigades, assigned three fallback signals and calculated that their stand would hold Ysmark’s Pale Wolf recovery routes long enough for Wuyue’s wounded to clear the pass.

Mo read the page and tore it in half.

[[speaker:jin]]“That copy was authenticated.”

[[speaker:mo]]“Then authenticate a better one.”

The imperial centre waited beneath sleet. Fifty-two thousand had crossed into Isgard. Months of fighting had reduced every formation, but the people standing behind Mo still wore the royal seal. They were not anonymous weight he could hide inside Jin’s arithmetic.

[[speaker:jin]]“If Ysmark restores the isolated banners, the pass closes on three armies.”

[[speaker:mo]]“Then tell my citizens what their position buys and let the brigades rotate. Your schedule becomes slower. They remain alive long enough to understand the order.”

[[speaker:jin]]“The delay gives Solveig another genuine trail.”

[[speaker:mo]]“Then stop leaving such interesting tea behind.”

Jin looked at the cup beside his abandoned map.

[[speaker:jin]]“That criticism is unrelated.”

[[speaker:mo]]“It has followed us across a continent.”

The revised withdrawal took six hours longer. Mo addressed the rear brigades himself. He told them the Pale Wolves would use every recovered soldier to reopen broken roads. He told them the rotation could fail. He did not call survival guaranteed because honesty had become inconvenient.

They held by companies instead of one doomed body. Paper orders changed colour with every rotation. Lantern codes expired after three uses. The rear line bent without becoming the grave Jin’s cleaner plan required.

Meanwhile, returned Ysmark prisoners walked into Freya’s camp under no Wuyue guard. They carried Duskvein pursuit ledgers proving their missing companies had been redirected through forged Skeldran evidence. Wuyue had captured them, treated them and released them with names the coalition had already recorded as dead.

Freya suspended Pale Wolf recovery operations and demanded an internal hearing. She did not forgive Wuyue. She stopped allowing grief to perform someone else’s work.

Solveig found Jin’s genuine trail before sunset. **No Footprint Survives the Last Snow** propagated through every false route and closed upon the command shelter where his pulse had last remained long enough to be read.

The tea was still warm.

Jin was gone.

Mo’s rotating orders continued moving the imperial centre without him. Farther north, **Borrowed Future** had already shown Jin the one pursuit decision Solveig would never delegate: she would personally close the final trace.

When her Hunt entered the valley, **Thousand Lantern Cage** sealed both ridges. The formation did not defeat Solveig’s High Sovereign body. It trapped her assignment behind collapsing roads while the last imperial rotation cleared the pass.

Jin met Mo at the next command shelter.

[[speaker:jin]]“Your correction cost us a fortress.”

[[speaker:mo]]“How many citizens?”

[[speaker:jin]]“Three hundred twelve dead or missing instead of four thousand left by order.”

Mo closed his eyes once. The number was still three hundred twelve lives. It was also the difference between strategy and convenience.

Jin placed the torn order into the casualty ledger.

[[speaker:jin]]“Keep correcting me.”

title: Liang Opens the Vein; Yun Decides What Enters
text:
Halvek Veyrhald closed every road around Liang Yue without raising a wall.

Prepared seals beneath the valley turned direction itself into a military order. The northern road folded toward the western gate. The western gate returned riders to the slope they had left. The only open path narrowed each time White Vein physicians tried to carry a patient through it.

**Every Road Kneels Before the Gate** did not trap Liang by force alone. It made every correct movement arrive where Halvek had prepared to receive it.

Yun Shizhen tasted the air and spat blood into the snow.

[[speaker:yun]]“No poison.”

[[speaker:liang]]“You sound disappointed.”

[[speaker:yun]]“Offended. Roads should not be smug.”

Liang released silver circulation threads through the nearest seal. **White Blood: Vein Whisper** entered the prepared route as though the road were an external meridian. For one instant she felt the network beneath the valley: twelve closures, three redirected bridges and Halvek himself standing at their shared pulse.

He struck before she could complete the reading.

Peak Sovereign pressure drove through her guard. Liang divided the first impact across false circulation branches, but the road seal changed the exit beneath her foot. Halvek’s spear passed through her side.

Yun’s hand reached the wound before the second thrust reached Liang’s heart. A clear compound burst across the blood and hardened into a nonlethal meridian fog. It did not poison Halvek. It made the open route between spear and target impossible to read for half a breath.

That half-breath saved Wuyue’s number two.

Liang pressed two fingers against the spear shaft and sent Vein Whisper deeper. Halvek felt the intrusion, severed the entire road and abandoned three prepared seals to keep her from learning the rest. The valley shuddered as the discarded route collapsed.

He retained nine roads. Liang retained one fragment of their circulation rhythm and a hole through her body.

[[speaker:yun]]“We leave.”

[[speaker:liang]]“I have the seam.”

[[speaker:yun]]“You have blood in your lung.”

[[speaker:liang]]“Both statements can be true.”

Yun placed a second compound beneath Liang’s tongue and signalled the extraction team. She did not pretend medicine had defeated Halvek. His network remained. His body remained stronger. The road Liang opened had been cut away before it could become a delayed victory.

White Vein soldiers carried their Sovereign through the one passage Yun’s fog made uncertain. Halvek let them leave because pursuing through an unreadable medical compound risked the road seals he still controlled.

Beyond the valley, Liang woke beneath Luo’s treatment needles.

[[speaker:liang]]“How much did we lose?”

[[speaker:yun]]“The road.”

[[speaker:liang]]“And gain?”

Yun placed the copied circulation fragment beside her.

[[speaker:yun]]“One seam too small for you to use alone.”

Liang studied it. Two thousand specialists were crossing the Black Current: four hundred trained to enter command circulation and sixteen hundred trained to hold overlapping suppression fields.

One seam was too small for a wounded Sovereign.

It might be large enough for an army designed to become a needle.

title: Kael Leaves the Perfect Wall
text:
Rimewall’s eastern fortress had never been breached.

Kael Veyran abandoned it while its gates still stood.

Norrvek siege chains had closed around the Silver Horizon Sect beyond the eastern exit. Mobile walls advanced behind the chains, separating three thousand swordswomen from the retreat road one section at a time. Solvane lances waited in the snow behind them.

Sigrun Veyrhald stood at the fortress centre. The boundary she had accepted grew heavier with every impact Kael delivered. **The First Wall Outlives the Siege** turned his committed force into additional structure. His torso had healed beneath Rhen’s art after her prepared ambush, but healing did not erase the memory inside movement. His weapon arm still changed angle before the old fracture demanded it.

A signal reached him from Arin.

Not a plea.

**EASTERN CHAINS CLOSING. FIELD DISCIPLES INSIDE.**

Sigrun lowered her shield.

[[speaker:sigrun]]“Leave this wall and you do not take it back.”

Kael felt the perfect geometry of Rimewall beneath his feet. If he remained, the central fortress could hold another day. If he crossed east, Norrvek would occupy the structure behind him and turn it against Wuyue.

[[speaker:kael]]“Walls can be surrendered.”

He withdrew **The Mountain Does Not Move** from the centre. Sigrun’s pressure filled the absence instantly. Veyrhald standards rose over an unbroken gate.

Kael did not look back.

Arin’s sect had already cut through the first chain layer when he reached the eastern road. **When the Silver Horizon Breaks** crossed the siege field in one immaculate line, severing axles, locking pins and command ropes without passing through the crews trapped between them. Five hundred inner disciples widened the seam. Field disciples carried wounded through it while senior matrons held Solvane’s lances away from the opening.

Then the second Norrvek wall closed.

Kael struck its centre with **Nine Heavens Collapse**. The mobile fortress folded inward. Arin turned the falling plates into cover and sent three cohorts beneath them.

[[speaker:arin]]“The central wall?”

[[speaker:kael]]“Sigrun’s.”

Arin did not tell him he had chosen correctly. She knew what the choice cost and respected it too much to make it painless.

[[speaker:arin]]“Then this road must be worth a fortress.”

They opened one passage together. Kael held Solvane’s approaching pressure. Arin cut chains until blood ran through the hand around her sword. Neither pursued when Norrvek withdrew the surviving engines. Their objective was not revenge. It was the moving line of disciples behind them.

The final Silver Horizon cohort crossed as Rimewall’s eastern gate closed beneath Veyrhald control.

Kael stood outside the fortress he could have held.

Beside him, Arin counted how few formations had answered the withdrawal signal.

title: Six Hundred Eleven Swords Still Stand
text:
Arin counted the Silver Horizon Sect at dawn.

She began with the people still standing.

Six hundred eleven swordswomen could hold formation. Some had bandages beneath armour. Some leaned upon their swords when officers looked elsewhere. All answered their names.

The second count found one thousand four hundred eighty-six alive but unable to stand in the line. Wounded. Unconscious. Meridian-damaged. Hands broken around sword grips that physicians had needed to cut away. Senior matrons lay beside field disciples. Inner-school badges purchased no earlier treatment.

The third count contained nine hundred three names.

Dead or missing.

Arin read every one aloud. Snow gathered on the shoulders of the six hundred eleven who remained standing. Kael waited outside the formation with his weapon grounded. He had trained Arin. He had not trained this complete sect, and grief did not grant him ownership of its silence.

At name two hundred fourteen, an instructor found her daughter among the missing and did not leave her place. At name four hundred eighty, two field disciples realized the same sword matron had carried both from the Norrvek chains. At name seven hundred, Arin’s voice failed once.

She drank water and continued.

When the final name entered the snow, one of the inner disciples stepped forward.

“Do we still call ourselves a sword sect?”

Arin looked beyond her. Three thousand had left home. The standing body before her was smaller than the inner school that once occupied one protected courtyard.

Behind them, the wounded had already begun working. One disciple who could no longer close her right hand was copying casualty routes with her left. A swordsmith with damaged meridians repaired armour buckles. Two matrons unable to circulate were organizing litters. The sect had ceased to function as a three-thousand-person army. It had not ceased to exist.

[[speaker:arin]]“Can you still choose what your sword protects?”

“Yes.”

[[speaker:arin]]“Then stand if you can. Serve another way if you cannot. Nobody disappears because the battlefield changed the work available to her.”

Kael approached only after the formation opened for him.

[[speaker:kael]]“The retreat road closes in two hours.”

[[speaker:arin]]“We need three.”

[[speaker:kael]]“Then it closes in three.”

He moved to the rear line. The world’s public number one did not offer to avenge the sect or erase the commanders who had shattered it. He lifted the heaviest broken siege plate and carried it into the barricade protecting the wounded.

Arin tied nine hundred three empty sword belts along the road out of Rimewall.

The wind moved through the buckles.

Six hundred eleven swords remained upright to hear them.

title: Lei Runs Where Luo Can Still Reach
text:
The white medical road refused to remain in one place.

Every time Eirholt marked a safe corridor, Raska Dravaryn’s cavalry redirected pressure toward its next junction. She did not strike the healers directly. She attacked the roads feeding them until neutrality became an island surrounded by wounded people who could not reach it.

Lei Zhen turned the island into a moving line.

He crossed between casualty stations in thunderfire bursts, carrying signal frames, physicians and groups of patients whose litters could not outrun the closing cavalry. Each movement burned another bright channel through meridians already damaged beneath Maedra’s Crimson Road.

Luo Wen met him at the fourth station with twelve needles between his fingers.

[[speaker:luo]]“Sit.”

[[speaker:lei]]“Busy.”

[[speaker:luo]]“Collapse, then. I can treat you more conveniently when you stop moving.”

Lei sat.

Luo placed needles along the old wound beneath his ribs. Maedra’s claimed road had vanished when her Domain contracted, but the internal damage remained. Thunderfire kept trying to use the shortest repaired route. Each crossing reopened it from within.

Raska’s next charge struck the outer station before Luo finished. **Crimson Cavalry Crosses the Setting Sun** preserved the force of one completed assault inside the next. Shield formations broke under momentum earned miles away.

Lei rose with four needles still in place.

[[speaker:luo]]“If you tear that channel again, I cannot keep returning it to you.”

[[speaker:lei]]“How many at the outer station?”

[[speaker:luo]]“Nine hundred patients. Two hundred staff.”

Lei vanished.

He did not challenge Raska for the honour of stopping her personally. **Storm King’s Calculation** found the cavalry rhythm connecting the completed charge to its successor. Lei broke the road beneath the formation at the one point that forced Raska to spend stored momentum protecting her own riders.

The interval lasted eleven breaths.

Long enough for Luo’s physicians to move the critical ward. Long enough for imperial infantry to inherit the corridor. Not long enough for Lei to win.

Raska’s spear caught his shoulder as he withdrew. Thunderfire carried him back to the white road instead of deeper into the duel.

Luo removed the bent needles without comment.

A signal arrived from the coast. Rui’s fleet road was closing.

Lei looked west. The distance was possible for him and impossible for the patients surrounding them.

[[speaker:luo]]“The imperial line can hold this corridor now.”

[[speaker:lei]]“Can it reach your next station?”

[[speaker:luo]]“Because you moved it, yes.”

Lei let Luo rebuild the damaged channel one final time. Ordinary soldiers took the white-road markers from his hands. Physicians began moving without requiring the Fourth Sovereign to carry every stretcher.

Only when the corridor continued without him did Lei turn toward Rui.

He ran where Luo could still reach him.

title: The Sea and the Crown Are Separated
text:
Rui and Ilyra understood Eldran’s trap at the same moment.

That did not give either of them permission to ignore it.

The Crownless Host’s southern cohorts collapsed first. Three command lanterns went dark. Shield Wing reports described thousands trapped beneath a cinder-heated ridge where retreating formations had begun burning through their own boots. Ilyra turned one meridian system toward them.

At the coast, twelve thousand Azure Riverlands soldiers and six hospital vessels discovered Norrvek shore engines closing the sea channel. Rui’s frozen road cracked beneath sustained heat. If he released it, the hospitals would ground within spear range.

Eldran Dravaryn raised the Cinder Standard between the two disasters. Ground his armoured infantry had held retained pressure and marching rhythm. Every captured mile strengthened the next.

[[speaker:rui]]“The cohort collapse is too clean.”

[[speaker:ilyra]]“The hospital timing is too exact.”

They stood back-to-back for one breath while the battlefield demanded opposite directions. Ilyra’s Shield Wing could absorb the ridge pressure. Rui’s control of water could keep the sea road alive. Either could follow the other and preserve their partnership. Doing so would abandon thousands who could not survive the separation.

[[speaker:ilyra]]“He studied us.”

[[speaker:rui]]“Then let him learn why the choice still works.”

Ilyra ran south. Rui ran west.

The false collapse contained real soldiers. Dravaryn had broken the support ridge beneath two Crownless cohorts and driven heated pressure through the ground. Ilyra opened **Crownless Mirror**, switched martial bodies inside the descending force and placed Shield Wing between the collapse and the people still crawling free. Returning Wing began converting the received pressure into an escape road.

At the shore, Rui froze the sea beneath the hospital fleet. Kharvorn engines drove iron anchors through the ice. Solvane lances struck each fracture before Rui could distribute it. He held the route anyway.

Eldran watched both fronts from the captured mile.

His victory was not forcing two Sovereigns apart. It was ensuring that once separated, each faced an objective too important to leave.

Ilyra’s signal reached Rui through broken lantern code.

**COHORTS ALIVE. CANNOT RETURN.**

Rui answered while one hospital ship cleared the outer anchor.

**FLEET MOVING. DO NOT RETURN.**

The last line of shared defence disappeared between them. Six Sovereign signatures moved toward the coast.

Rui felt them coming.

He could leave before they closed. The hospital ships could not.

He placed both hands against the broken sea and made the frozen road hold.

title: Six Sovereigns Close the Water
text:
Six Sovereigns surrounded Shen Rui after the fifth hospital ship escaped.

Eldran Dravaryn held the centre beneath **Cinder Standard Over the Fallen Mile**. Brynja Kharvorn controlled the shore engines. Oskar Solvane sealed the northern retreat with winterglass lances. Kellan Haldren had returned only with the Ash-Horn companies still bound to defend Veyrhald’s lawful coast, not Maedra’s Hearth order. Two Dravaryn captains closed the remaining angles.

None was as strong as Rui alone.

Together, they had studied every road he maintained during the first year of war.

The Sixth Sovereign struck the southern ice. Kharvorn anchors caught the fracture. Solvane lances forced the break toward the fleet. Rui redirected it beneath himself and rebuilt the hospital route instead.

The sixth ship turned south.

A signal officer on its rear deck raised the clear marker. All patients were beyond the engine range.

Rui could finally withdraw.

Eldran’s captured mile released a year of prepared heat through the ice behind him. The retreat path became water. Haldren spears received Rui’s first counter without trying to defeat it; the two Dravaryn captains used that committed motion to enter from opposite sides.

Rui raised **Sea Without Shore**. Water, ice and mist became one circulating battlefield. Kharvorn’s western engines froze inside their own mechanisms. Solvane lost three lance lines beneath rising water. One Dravaryn captain fell with his meridians locked in ice.

Then Eldran planted the Cinder Standard again.

Every foot of shore the coalition still possessed answered him. Heat entered Rui’s field from below instead of contesting its surface. Haldren’s reserve formation held the centre long enough for Kharvorn to break the frozen engines free. Solvane’s next line struck the exact road Rui had used to supply the hospitals for eight months.

The ice shattered.

Rui remained standing on water.

Five Sovereigns attacked while the sixth rebuilt the field they needed. He stopped Brynja’s axe, redirected Oskar’s lance and froze one captain’s circulation before Kellan’s spear formation struck his back. Eldran’s armoured pressure landed through the shore beneath him.

Rui could still flee across open sea.

Behind him, the last hospital vessel had not yet cleared the distant current. Its hull carried no formation capable of surviving pursuit.

He closed the water instead. A wall of moving ice rose between the ship and every Isgard technique.

Six systems fell upon the Fifth Sovereign at once.

The watching fleet saw Rui disappear beneath broken water, cinder pressure and spear light.

The hospital vessel reached the southern current.

Only then did his frozen wall fall.

title: Every Time Rui Rises
text:
Rui stood after his left leg stopped carrying weight.

Eldran struck him back into the ruined shore.

The first fall broke the ice armour around Rui’s ribs. The second broke the circulation route feeding his right arm. By the third, Kharvorn’s engines had withdrawn from range because they were no longer needed. Six Sovereign systems had become a ring around one exhausted man.

Rui rose again.

Not because he expected to win. The Azure Riverlands fleet could still see him. Thousands of soldiers had maintained his roads through two winters. If their commander vanished beneath the first complete defeat, panic would dissolve the water formations protecting the retreat.

Oskar’s lance drove through Rui’s shoulder and pinned him against a broken engine plate. Rui froze the shaft, shattered it and forced himself upright.

Eldran kicked him across the shore.

Each time Rui stood, another Sovereign put him down before the fleet could mistake endurance for reversal. Haldren formations broke his barriers. Dravaryn pressure crushed the repaired channels beneath his sternum. Brynja’s axe struck the ground beside his head and sent iron force through the bones already fractured there.

The beating continued after victory because Eldran needed the fleet to believe its Sovereign had become helpless.

Rui’s soldiers began losing rhythm. The outer water line collapsed. Two transports drifted toward Isgard anchors.

Thunder split the coast.

Lei Zhen crossed eleven miles in one burning interval and landed inside the ring. His meridians tore along the path Luo had warned him not to reopen. He did not attack Eldran. He did not spend one breath proving the Fourth Sovereign could punish the people surrounding the Fifth.

He lifted Rui.

Eldran’s standard drove pressure through the shore. Lei took it across his back and converted the surviving force into movement. Solvane lances closed the air ahead. Lei broke one line, accepted the second through his thigh and ran.

Rui’s eyes opened against his shoulder.

[[speaker:rui]]“Fleet?”

[[speaker:lei]]“South.”

[[speaker:rui]]“I can stand.”

[[speaker:lei]]“You have demonstrated that enough.”

Luo met them four miles from Rhen’s range. Rui’s circulation had become one failing thread. Luo placed his staff beneath Lei’s arm and ran beside them while working: one needle into the heart route, two beneath the damaged lung, a palm against the dantian to keep the final current from scattering.

[[speaker:luo]]“Eleven miles.”

[[speaker:lei]]“I know.”

[[speaker:luo]]“If you fall, I cannot carry both of you.”

[[speaker:lei]]“Then complain faster.”

Behind them, Eldran did not pursue beyond the captured mile. He had achieved the image he wanted.

Ahead, the first frozen petals appeared in the rain.

Lei ran until the man in his arms crossed into Rhen’s reach.

title: Sanctuary Restores a Body, Not an Army
text:
Rhen opened **Sanctuary of Petals** before Lei reached the retreat corridor.

A pale hemisphere crossed the road, the casualty fields and the shattered columns still moving out of Rimewall. Isgard pressure struck its surface and stopped. Inside, frozen petals passed through armour, mud and blood without disturbing either.

Lei carried Rui across the boundary.

The Fifth Sovereign had almost no stable circulation. His meridians had collapsed in six separate regions. Bones had broken through healed fractures. One lung no longer opened. Luo’s final needle held the heart route together by a thread thin enough that ordinary movement could end it.

Rhen placed one hand over Rui’s sternum.

**Sanctuary of Petals** restored the body in the order life required, not the order pride would have chosen. The heart route stabilized. The lung opened. Broken bones returned to alignment. Torn meridians re-formed and strengthened around the memory of what had destroyed them.

Across the hemisphere, thousands received the same impossible mercy. Soldiers who had entered on litters sat upright. Physicians watched wounds close beneath hands that had been too tired to continue. Lei’s burned movement channels repaired before he could collapse. Luo’s exhausted circulation steadied without erasing the decisions that had exhausted it.

Rui woke.

He did not ask who had defeated the six Sovereigns for him. Nobody had.

[[speaker:rui]]“Hospital ships?”

[[speaker:lei]]“All six escaped.”

Rui closed his eyes. One breath left him that was not pain.

Outside the Sanctuary, the sea road remained lost. Wrecked transports burned along the coast. Soldiers Rhen had never reached remained dead. The Silver Horizon Sect still carried nine hundred three empty sword belts. Healing restored Rui’s ability to stand; it did not return command automatically to officers who had kept the fleet alive while believing him broken.

Sera entered through the western edge with casualty ledgers beneath one arm. She had spent the retreat moving between five roads, closing whichever fracture threatened to become a collapse, never pretending one body could occupy every front.

[[speaker:sera]]“Rimewall is abandoned. Haldren withdrew from Maedra’s function. Ysmark suspended recovery operations. We lost the central fortress, the eastern wall and the sea corridor.”

Jin arrived behind her. His map now held fewer coalition banners and far less Wuyue ground.

[[speaker:jin]]“We are winning the structure.”

Rui looked toward the wounded filling the Sanctuary.

[[speaker:rui]]“It does not feel like winning.”

[[speaker:jin]]“It should not.”

Rhen removed his hand only when Rui’s circulation sustained itself.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You are healed. You are not rested.”

[[speaker:rui]]“How long?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Longer if you argue.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He means that literally.”

The Black March left Rimewall beneath an indestructible garden of frozen petals. It carried a physically restored Sovereign, a sword sect no longer able to field an army and tens of thousands fewer fighting bodies than it had brought north.

Behind them, Isgard raised banners over the fortress.

On Jin’s map, two smaller supports had already disappeared.
